blocks.raw: <Tip>De Stijl = primary colors (R, Y, B) + orthogonal geometry (right angles only) + white space = universal harmony. Schröder House exemplifies this: interpenetrating planes, primary colors, movable walls, minimal ornament. Remember: De Stijl is a unified philosophy across painting (Mondrian) and architecture (Rietveld).</Tip>

blocks.raw: <Note>All three movements rejected ornament and tradition and pursued abstraction. But they differ fundamentally: De Stijl sought universal harmony through systematic reduction to primary colors, right angles, and white space. Constructivism pursued technological power and revolutionary ideals through asymmetrical, dynamic forms. Expressionism pursued emotional intensity through sculptural, wave-like, organic-inspired abstract forms. This distinction is testable—you must know all three and their differences.</Note>

blocks.raw: <Warn>Critical: Don't confuse these movements. (1) De Stijl is NOT Constructivism—De Stijl is orderly and symmetric with primary colors; Constructivism is asymmetrical and dynamic without color orthodoxy. The Tatlin Tower is NOT De Stijl. (2) Expressionism is NOT naturalism or Art Nouveau—it's abstract and sculptural, pursuing emotional intensity through geometric distortion, not nature-imitation. (3) The Tatlin Tower is unbuilt (1919–1920)—its significance lies in the revolutionary idea, not a completed building.</Warn>
